name: Triple Zero (000)
summary: Primary emergency number for Police, Fire or Ambulance; calls are free.
caution: Use for emergencies only. A mobile cannot reach the Emergency Call Service where there is no coverage from any mobile network.

name: Emergency Relay Service / National Relay Service (NRS)
summary: Accessible emergency-call pathways for people who are d/Deaf or have hearing or speech difficulty. Use 106 from a TTY/TDD; it is not a general text-message number.
hours: NRS is available 24/7 except Video Relay; Video Relay hours are limited.
caution: Video Relay is not recommended for emergency calls: it cannot be identified/prioritised as emergency and operates only limited hours. Internet/mobile-based relay may be less reliable than 106 and may not identify caller/location. For a TTY, dial 106 first.

name: NSW State Emergency Service (NSW SES)
summary: Emergency assistance for flood, storm or tsunami, including storm/wind/fallen-tree damage. Requests are prioritised.
caution: If anyone is trapped or injured, call 000. The online contact form is not monitored for storm/flood emergencies; call 132 500.

name: Police Assistance Line
summary: Non-urgent police assistance, minor-crime reporting and general enquiries.
caution: For emergencies or a crime in progress, call 000 instead.

name: Poisons Information Centre
summary: Expert phone advice for suspected exposure to poisons, including medicines, chemicals, cleaning products, bites and stings.
caution: Call promptly; do not wait for symptoms. If someone has stopped breathing or collapsed, call 000 for an ambulance.

name: healthdirect helpline
summary: Health advice from a registered nurse for any health concern.
caution: For urgent medical help, call 000.

name: Lifeline crisis support
summary: Confidential crisis support with a trained crisis supporter; text is also available at 0477 13 11 14.
caution: If life is in danger, call 000.

name: 1800RESPECT
summary: National counselling, information and support for people impacted by domestic, family or sexual violence. Text: 0458 737 732; online chat and video call are also offered.
caution: If in immediate danger, call 000. Use a safer device if possible: calls, texts and browsing can leave records. This directory has no quick-exit feature and does not erase browsing history.

name: Kids Helpline
summary: Free, confidential phone and online-chat counselling for children and young people aged 5–25.

name: NSW Mental Health Line
summary: Free statewide advice, triage and connection to NSW Health mental health services; a trained professional completes a brief assessment and recommends appropriate care.
caution: Not a one-off counselling service. If someone is in immediate danger, call 000 or attend an emergency department.
language: For another language, call TIS National 131 450 and ask to be connected. Relay options are listed on the source page.

name: Service NSW — emergencies and natural disasters
summary: Disaster preparation/recovery information, personalised support pathways, relief/grants information and replacement-document help; includes support-hub information.
caution: In an emergency, call 000; for flood/storm/tsunami assistance, call NSW SES 132 500.

name: Temporary and emergency housing / Link2Home
summary: Link2Home helps people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. For disaster accommodation pathways, contact Service NSW on 13 77 88 or a recovery centre.

name: Legal Aid NSW — Disaster Response Legal Service
summary: Free legal help after bushfire, storm or flood: insurance claims/disputes, tenancy/housing, disaster grants, financial hardship, Centrelink, work rights and documents.

name: Bureau of Meteorology — NSW warnings summary
summary: Official current NSW weather-warning summary; automatically refreshes when warnings are issued.
caution: Read the linked warning in full and follow local emergency-service directions.

name: Bureau of Meteorology — national warning phone service
summary: Latest weather warnings by phone.

name: Live Traffic NSW
summary: Transport for NSW official real-time road incidents, closures and changed conditions; a text-to-speech Traffic Info Line and operator assistance are available.
caution: Always read individual incident advice/restrictions and do not drive into floodwater or a closed road.

name: NSW SES evacuation centres
summary: Current evacuation-centre locations and opening hours; the page also gives evacuation guidance.
caution: Centres open only during emergencies and status changes. Follow evacuation instructions immediately; check routes via Live Traffic. For fires, consult NSW RFS as directed by the page.

name: NSW SES accessibility resources
summary: Flood/storm/tsunami planning resources for low/no hearing or vision, disability/mobility, intellectual disability, mental health conditions, carers and Easy Read; includes Auslan and NRS information.
caution: Create a tailored plan and support network before an emergency; plan backup power/transport for life-sustaining and mobility equipment.

name: NSW SES — household pets emergency planning
summary: Pet evacuation planning and a 3–7-day animal emergency-kit checklist.
caution: Plan to take pets, but evacuation centres may not always be available or suitable for animals; arrange alternative safe options. Assistance animals have separate access guidance.

name: NSW SES — assistance animals emergency planning
summary: Planning guidance and kit checklist for assistance animals during evacuation.
caution: The NSW SES page says people should not be denied transport or evacuation-centre access because of an assistance animal; plan travel and specific animal needs in advance.

name: NSW Government — Get Ready Animals
summary: Emergency planning for companion animals, larger pets, horses and livestock, including a Pet Ready Plan.
caution: Plan safe animal transport and alternative accommodation early. Do not re-enter an unsafe area to retrieve an animal; follow emergency-service directions.

name: Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) pathway for NSW mental-health support
summary: Interpreter connection pathway: ask TIS to ring NSW Mental Health Line 1800 011 511.
caution: For immediate danger, call 000 rather than waiting for a support connection.

name: MyFirePlan
summary: NSW RFS online bushfire planning tool. Discuss your household’s leaving triggers, safer destination, routes and what to take before fire threatens.
caution: Leaving early is your safest choice. Do not wait for an official warning to decide when to leave. This tool is for planning, not incident warnings.

name: NSW Rural Fire Service
summary: Official NSW bushfire information, preparation resources and links to current incidents and fire danger ratings.

name: RFS Fires Near Me
summary: Official NSW RFS incident map and fire information. Read the incident advice and follow emergency-service instructions.
caution: Maps may not show every incident or update immediately. Do not wait for a mapped incident before taking protective action.

name: Fire danger ratings and total fire bans
summary: Check the fire danger rating and total fire ban status for your NSW fire area. A rating describes potential fire consequences; it is not a report that a fire has started.

name: RFS bushfire survival plan
summary: Official bushfire survival planning guidance to use with your household and MyFirePlan.

name: HazardWatch
summary: Official interactive hazard-warning map. NSW SES links to HazardWatch for current flood, severe weather and tsunami warnings.
caution: Check the displayed hazard coverage, location, issue time and full warning. A blank map or no displayed warnings does not mean your location is safe.

name: Hazards Near Me NSW
summary: Find the official Hazards Near Me app through the NSW emergency hub and set watch zones for relevant local emergencies.
caution: Keep more than one information channel. Do not rely on receiving an app notification before acting.

name: H5 bird flu — Australian Government
summary: Australian Government H5 bird flu hub: local advice, reporting, wildlife, pets, backyard birds, farms, human health and translated resources. The short address redirects to the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry campaign.
caution: If you notice sick or dead birds or other animals, do not touch them or get too close. Take photos only if safe, note the location and report it. This is animal-disease reporting, not a human medical emergency line.

name: Get Ready NSW
summary: Official preparation hub: understand your risk, make an emergency plan, pack a kit, know the warnings and plan with neighbours.

name: NSW SES — during an emergency
summary: Official flood, storm and tsunami response hub, with warnings, apps, evacuation information and links to safety guidance.

name: NSW Health — respiratory illness (flu, COVID-19 and RSV)
summary: NSW Health guidance on flu, COVID-19 and RSV: vaccination, staying home when unwell, wearing a mask if you must go out, testing before visiting people at higher risk, and links to weekly respiratory surveillance reports.
caution: This page covers prevention and vaccination, not symptom triage. For urgent medical help, call 000.

name: healthdirect — COVID-19
summary: healthdirect guide to COVID-19 vaccination, testing and symptoms.
caution: For urgent medical help, call 000. For advice from a registered nurse, use the healthdirect helpline.

name: Australian Government — influenza (flu) vaccine
summary: Australian Government Department of Health information on yearly flu vaccination, who is recommended to be vaccinated and which groups can get it free under the National Immunisation Program.

name: Australian Government — COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Australian Government Department of Health information on COVID-19 vaccines, including free vaccine eligibility under the National Immunisation Program.

name: NSW Health — immunisation programs
summary: NSW Health index to vaccination information by age and situation, including pregnancy, childhood, adult and older-adult programs, and flu, RSV, COVID-19 and travel vaccines.

name: NSW Health — infectious diseases
summary: NSW Health hub for infectious diseases: fact sheets, an A–Z of diseases, the weekly respiratory update, and outbreak alerts and guidance.

name: NSW Public Health Units
summary: Calling this number connects you automatically to your local NSW Health Public Health Unit. The source page also lists a Public Health Unit directory.
caution: Not an emergency or clinical advice line. The source does not state hours or whether the number is intended for the public or for clinicians. For personal health advice, call healthdirect or see a GP; for urgent medical help, call 000.

name: Victoria State Emergency Service (VICSES)
summary: Emergency help for flood, storm, tsunami and earthquake in Victoria. Requests to the help line are logged by a call centre and a local volunteer may follow up.
caution: If life is threatened, call 000. The website enquiry form is for general enquiries only, not emergencies. For minor leaks, superficial damage or debris removal, VICSES directs people to a tradesperson or insurer.

name: Country Fire Authority (CFA)
summary: Victoria's CFA site covers fire safety, fire bans and Fire Danger Ratings, and how to contact CFA districts and brigades across country Victoria.
caution: In an emergency dial 000 for fire, police or ambulance.

name: Fire Rescue Victoria (FRV)
summary: Contact page for Fire Rescue Victoria, the state's fire and rescue service. The page gives an enquiries form and links to its response area information.
caution: For fire and rescue, police or ambulance in an emergency, call 000. The page's general enquiries number is not an emergency line.

name: VicEmergency (website, app and hotline)
summary: Victoria's official emergency information service: a map and list of current incidents and warnings, watch zones for the VicEmergency app, and pages on preparing and recovering. This directory does not reproduce live warnings.
caution: The hotline is for emergency information, not emergencies. In an emergency call 000. The hotline is staffed Monday to Friday, 8.00am to 6.00pm, with opening times extended during significant bushfires; recorded information on specific topics is available 24 hours a day (CFA hotline page). Deaf, hearing or speech-impaired callers can use the National Relay Service; non-English speakers can ring 131 450 for translated information (as stated on the CFA hotline page).

name: Victoria Police Assistance Line
summary: Non-urgent police assistance, general enquiries and reporting a crime that has already occurred. Non-urgent crimes and events can also be reported online.
hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
caution: For danger or a crime in progress, call 000 instead.

name: Victorian Department of Health: infectious diseases
summary: The Victorian Department of Health's infectious diseases page: guidelines, notifiable conditions, an A-Z of disease information and links to surveillance reports. It is aimed mainly at health professionals and links to the Better Health Channel for consumer information.

name: Victorian Department of Health: mental health telephone and online services
summary: Department of Health list of mental health phone and online services. It describes area mental health triage as a 24/7 specialist response whose phone number differs by area, so there is no single statewide triage number.
caution: This is a directory, not a crisis line: the page lists no single statewide mental health triage number because area numbers differ.

name: SuicideLine Victoria (suicide crisis support)
summary: Suicide crisis support: free professional phone and online counselling for people living in Victoria, including people affected by suicide. Supported by the Victorian Government and delivered by Lifeline. It is not an area mental health triage line.
caution: If someone is in immediate danger or has seriously harmed themselves, call 000.

name: Relief and recovery in Victoria (Victorian Government)
summary: Victorian Government guide to help after major emergencies: relief centres, emergency accommodation and payments, clean-up and mental health support, with guides for bushfire, storm and flood. Emergency Management Victoria coordinates state and regional relief and recovery.

name: Queensland State Emergency Service (Queensland SES)
summary: Help for non-life-threatening flood and storm emergencies during severe weather. Request help by phone, online or through the SES Assistance QLD app.
caution: If life is in danger, call 000. 132 500 is for non-life-threatening flood and storm help.

name: Queensland Fire Department (QFD)
summary: State government page about Queensland's primary fire and emergency service, which includes Queensland Fire and Rescue and the volunteer Rural Fire Service Queensland (rural, semi-rural and urban-fringe areas, fire permits). The agency's own site could not be checked.
caution: For a fire or any emergency, call 000. The page lists only the general Queensland Government line (13 74 68) for enquiries, not a fire emergency number.

name: Queensland Disasters: current warnings
summary: Queensland Government page linking to official severe weather, flood, cyclone, bushfire, maritime and heat warning sources and local council disaster dashboards. It also offers machine-readable alert feeds and guidance on acting on warnings.

name: Policelink (Queensland Police non-urgent reporting and enquiries)
summary: State government page on Policelink, Queensland's phone and online reporting for police matters that are not emergencies, such as property damage, stealing, break-ins, stolen vehicles and lost property. The police service's own site could not be checked.
caution: For urgent matters or a crime in progress, call 000 instead. The number comes from a Queensland Government page; another Queensland Government page lists a different number, so confirm it on the police site if a call does not connect.

name: Queensland Health: health alerts
summary: State government listing of health alerts published by Queensland Health, each linking to its own page. Use it to find official public health information on outbreaks and other health risks. Queensland Health's own site could not be checked.
caution: A directory of alerts, not a dedicated infectious diseases page. For emergencies call 000.

name: 1300 MH CALL (Queensland mental health access line)
summary: Confidential mental health telephone triage line and first point of contact for Queensland public mental health services. It gives support, advice and referrals, including for mental health crises.
caution: Only available within Queensland. In an emergency call 000.

name: Queensland Government disaster recovery support
summary: Queensland Government information on financial help and support services after a disaster, including grants, event-specific funding pages and wellbeing contacts. The Community Recovery Hotline can give advice.
caution: Grants have eligibility criteria. For emergencies call 000.

name: WA State Emergency Service (SES) emergency assistance (DFES)
summary: In Western Australia the SES is delivered through the Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES). The DFES contact page lists the SES emergency assistance number for urgent property repairs you cannot manage yourself, such as storm or flood damage.
caution: Call 000 for fire or a life-threatening emergency. Requests are prioritised by urgency, so there may be waits during a natural disaster. The page says SES help does not cover fences, permanent repairs, debris clearing or basic repairs.

name: Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES)
summary: Western Australia's fire and emergency services agency. The site covers hazard information (bushfire, fire in the home, cyclone, storm, flood, tsunami, earthquake, hazmat), warning systems, the volunteer services and recovery funding.
caution: 13 33 37 is an information line. For fire or a life-threatening emergency call 000.

name: Emergency WA — Warnings and Incidents
summary: Western Australia's official site and app for emergency warnings and incident information, including Total Fire Bans and Fire Danger Ratings. The app lets you set watch zones and RSS and CAP feeds are available.
caution: The site says not to wait for an official message before acting, and that warnings may not be issued before life or property is threatened. Notifications may not arrive if an alert is outside your watch zone or your phone has Do Not Disturb or Battery Saver on. Call 000 in a life-threatening emergency.

name: WA Police Force — Contact WA Police (131 444)
summary: Non-emergency police contact: report a crime that has already happened, request police attendance or ask a general question. The page also lists TTY, SMS Assist (registration required) and Crime Stoppers contacts.
caution: In an emergency, or for an immediate threat to people or property, call 000. SMS Assist must be registered for first and must not be used for emergencies.

name: HealthyWA — Health conditions A to Z (WA Department of Health)
summary: Weak fit for infectious diseases: the HealthyWA conditions A to Z, the WA Department of Health's public information site. The index links to articles on many infectious diseases (for example influenza, measles, COVID-19, whooping cough and mosquito-borne diseases) and other conditions, but it is not a dedicated outbreak or public health page.
caution: General information only. For urgent symptoms call 000.

name: Mental Health Emergency Response Line (MHERL)
summary: A 24-hour phone service staffed by mental health clinicians for people in a mental health crisis, plus their families, carers and people who witness a crisis. Covers the Perth metropolitan area and Peel; regional and remote WA uses Rurallink.
caution: MHERL is not an emergency service. In an emergency call 000. Peel callers use 1800 676 822. Regional and remote WA callers should use Rurallink on 1800 552 002 (4:30pm to 8:30am on weeknights, 24 hours on weekends and public holidays), as the Mental Health Commission page states.

name: Recovery WA — Recovering from an Emergency (DFES)
summary: Western Australia's emergency recovery site run by DFES. It lists recovery pages for individual emergencies, information on the Premier's Relief Payment and guidance on recovering from bushfire, storm, cyclone, flood and other hazards.
caution: What help is available depends on the emergency and whether assistance has been activated; check the site for current eligibility.

name: South Australian State Emergency Service (SA SES)
summary: Official SA SES contact page. Lists 132 500 for SA SES emergency assistance (flood and storm) and an infoline for incident information during significant weather events.
caution: For life-threatening emergencies call 000. The online contact form does not start an SA SES response; call 132 500 for help.

name: South Australian Country Fire Service (CFS) — Incidents & warnings
summary: Official CFS incidents and warnings page. Explains the warning levels and incident categories used in CFS listings and links to bushfire preparedness information. It also lists the CFS Information Hotline.
caution: The Information Hotline is for information, not emergencies. In an emergency call 000.

name: SAFECOM — Emergency Information (Alert SA)
summary: Official SAFECOM page explaining how South Australia's public emergency warnings work, including the Alert SA platform, Emergency Alert, the bushfire Advice and warning levels, accessibility options and other recommended information sources.
caution: Do not rely on a single source: check Alert SA, local ABC radio and the CFS and SES channels, as communications can be unreliable during emergencies.

name: Tasmania State Emergency Service (Tasmania SES)
summary: Tasmania SES contact page: the emergency help line for flood, storm and tsunami, general enquiries, and relay and interpreter options.
caution: In a life-threatening emergency call Triple Zero (000). The 132 500 line is described only for flood, storm and tsunami emergencies.

name: Tasmania Fire Service (TFS)
summary: Tasmania's fire service site: fire danger ratings, fire bans and permits, bushfire and home fire safety guidance, and links to incidents and warnings.
caution: The Information Line is not for emergencies. Report a fire on 000.

name: TasALERT
summary: The Tasmanian Government's official emergency information site and app, carrying warnings from agencies such as Tasmania Fire Service, Tasmania Police and SES, with a map and preparedness guidance.
caution: In a life-threatening emergency call 000.

name: Tasmania Police: Police Assistance Line
summary: Tasmania Police contact page for non-emergency police assistance and online reporting of some matters.
caution: For a life-threatening emergency, if you are in danger, or if a crime is in progress, call Triple Zero (000). TTY users dial 106.

name: TasRECOVERY (TasALERT recovery pages)
summary: The Tasmanian Government's recovery information after emergencies, with topic pages on financial assistance, health and wellbeing, insurance, legal matters, animal welfare, and your land and home.

name: ACT State Emergency Service (ACT SES)
summary: Contact page for the ACT State Emergency Service, part of the ACT Emergency Services Agency. Lists the storm and flood assistance line for emergency help during floods or storms.
phoneLabel: 132 500 — ACT SES storm and flood assistance
caution: For a life-threatening emergency, call 000. The page states no hours for 132 500.

name: ACT Fire & Rescue
summary: ACT Emergency Services Agency page for ACT Fire & Rescue, the territory's urban fire and rescue service, with its community programs and Community Fire Units. Grass and bushfire response is covered by the ACT Rural Fire Service.
caution: In a life-threatening emergency call 000. The ESA contact page says not to call fire stations to report an emergency.

name: ACT Rural Fire Service (ACT RFS)
summary: ACT Emergency Services Agency page for the ACT Rural Fire Service, which protects the ACT community from grass and bushfires, with preparation information and links to fire danger ratings and total fire ban pages.
caution: In a life-threatening emergency call 000.

name: ACT Emergency Services Agency: warnings and alerts
summary: Explains how ACT emergency warnings are issued and where to find them: the ESA website and incidents map, the Hazards Near Me app, social media, ABC Local Radio, AusAlert and Emergency Alert messages. Describes the channels only; no live warnings.

name: ACT Policing: Police Assistance Line
summary: Australian Federal Police contact page with an ACT Policing section giving the Police Assistance Line for non-urgent police assistance, which connects callers to local police in the ACT.
caution: In an emergency, call 000 and ask for police. This number is taken from the Australian Federal Police contact page because ACT Policing's own site could not be checked.

name: ACT Health: diseases and conditions
summary: ACT Government index of infectious diseases and conditions, linking to pages on topics such as measles, influenza, COVID-19 and mpox. Managed by the Health and Community Services Directorate. It is a general index, not a dedicated public health contact page.
caution: The page says its content is intended for health professionals and is not personal medical advice; see your own health provider about a health concern.

name: Access Mental Health Line (Canberra Health Services)
summary: Phone support for anyone concerned about their own or someone else's mental health, including carers and health professionals. Gives information and advice and can refer to urgent mental health assessment or other Canberra Health Services.
hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (Access Mental Health Line)
caution: Not for life-threatening emergencies: call 000 immediately.

name: ACT Government: support after an emergency
summary: ACT Government starting point for recovery: immediate relief, insurance, financial aid, legal help, replacing lost documents and mental health support. Support varies by emergency and is updated after an event.
caution: The page says immediate relief is generally time-limited (up to about three months) and that eligibility depends on the emergency.

name: NT Emergency Service (NTES)
summary: Help from the NT Emergency Service during floods, storms or cyclones, plus headquarters contacts and an email address for general enquiries. NTES is part of NT Police, Fire and Emergency Services.
caution: The official page says to save 000 for other emergencies. Headquarters numbers (Northern 08 8922 3630, Southern 08 8951 9300) are listed under business hours, not for emergencies.

name: NT Fire and Rescue Service (NTFRS)
summary: NT Fire and Rescue Service responds to fires, road crash rescues and hazardous materials incidents. The site has bushfire safety guidance, permits to burn, fire station profiles and a fire incident map.
hours: 24 hours (listed under 24 hour assistance lines for non-emergencies)
caution: This number is for non-emergency fire assistance only. In an emergency always dial 000.

name: NTFRS Fire Incident Map
summary: Interactive map of NT Fire and Rescue Service incidents and bushfire warning levels, published by NT Police, Fire and Emergency Services.
caution: Partial coverage only: this is a fire-focused incident map, not an all-hazards warnings site, and it is not real time (the page says it updates roughly every 10 to 15 minutes and advises using more than one source). It does not cover flood, storm or cyclone warnings. In an emergency call 000.

name: NT Police Force: police contacts
summary: Police assistance where there is no immediate danger, with local station numbers and other police contacts.
hours: 24 hours (listed under 24 hour assistance lines for non-emergencies)
caution: For non-emergencies only. In an emergency or life-threatening situation call 000.
